stories.headline: Trump DOJ report: Garland’s school-board memo drew internal alarm, with one official calling it an ‘Anti-MAGA Task Force’
stories.summary: The Justice Department on Monday released its “Report to Expose the Weaponization of Government Against Parents in Schools,” plus hundreds of exhibits and emails about then-Attorney General Merrick Garland’s October 2021 memo directing the FBI and U.S. attorneys to address threats against school boards. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said the records show the Garland DOJ worked with White House officials and the National School Boards Association to chill parents’ free speech. The report says the memo met sustained internal pushback: one deputy assistant attorney general wrote that Garland “might as well rename the damn thing the Anti-MAGA Task Force,” the Public Integrity Section chief called the proposal “stupid,” and FBI and Civil Rights Division officials warned that much of the parents’ activity was protected by the First Amendment.

stories.headline: Biden-appointed judge tosses a noncitizen-voting case, ruling the federal ban on foreigners voting unconstitutional
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz in Miami dismissed the federal case against Chelsea Cox, a Jamaican national who overstayed a 1999 tourist visa and is accused of using a fake U.S. Virgin Islands birth certificate to get a Florida license and vote in the 2012, 2016, 2018 and 2020 elections. Siding with the defense, Leibowitz ruled that the text and original meaning of the Constitution give states, not Congress, the power to set voter qualifications, so 18 U.S.C. § 611, the federal ban on noncitizens voting in federal races, is unconstitutional. He wrote that one can assume Cox committed every element of the crime but she “cannot be prosecuted” under an unconstitutional statute, while noting Florida itself can still prohibit and punish the same conduct. The ruling lands weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: Sen. Thom Tillis calls his vote to confirm Hegseth the ‘biggest regret of my career’ in a new book
stories.summary: North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis writes in “How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents,” out Tuesday, that casting the deciding vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in January 2025 is the “biggest regret of my career,” and that he also “should’ve stopped” Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from becoming health secretary. Tillis, who is not seeking reelection after breaking with Trump over the big tax-and-spending bill, says he can count at least 30 GOP colleagues who privately voice reservations about the president but praise him on camera. He mostly spares Trump himself, writing that “my beef is not with him, but the idiots he’s got working for him.”

stories.headline: Supreme Court won’t hear a Michigan mom’s challenge to a school ban on ‘Let’s Go Brandon’ sweatshirts
stories.summary: The justices on Monday turned away an appeal from a Michigan mother whose two sons were told to take off “Let’s Go Brandon” sweatshirts she bought them for Christmas in 2022. A lower court had ruled that the phrase’s veiled vulgarity, a stand-in for an obscene chant aimed at Joe Biden, lets schools ban it. Her lawyers argued the phrase contains no swear words and that the decision gives school officials wide latitude to squelch political speech based on their own sense of what is vulgar; the district said lewd messages have no place in school even when political. The phrase dates to a 2021 NASCAR race, when a TV reporter described the crowd’s chant as “Let’s go, Brandon” for winning driver Brandon Brown.

stories.headline: White House bars Politico from Air Force One on the day it was set to serve as the print pool
stories.summary: The White House refused to let Politico aboard Air Force One on Monday, when the outlet was scheduled to be the print pool reporter responsible for sending dispatches from the plane to other news organizations. The administration earlier kept CNN off the plane during its turn in the TV pool, swapping in LindellTV and Real America’s Voice on recent flights. President Trump announced Sept. 18 that he was banning Politico, CNN and MS NOW from the White House over what he called “fake news”; a judge temporarily blocked that ban and restored the reporters’ access, and legal experts have called it a First Amendment violation.

stories.headline: State Department warns visa holders after a UC Berkeley ‘Kirkversary’ party mocked Charlie Kirk’s memorial
stories.summary: On Sept. 10, the first anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s assassination, Turning Point USA members at UC Berkeley held a solemn memorial with a large portrait of Kirk; a few hours later, the Daily Californian reported, a crowd gathered for a “Kirkversary” to sing, cheer and boo at Kirk’s memory. After photos of attendees circulated online, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott told The College Fix that people on visas “are guests in this country” and the administration “will not tolerate” visa holders who break the law, support terrorism or incite violence. TPUSA chapter president John Paul Leon said supporting political violence against Kirk “is an act of moral depravity.” It is unclear whether any attendees are actually on student visas.

stories.headline: Mexico’s Sheinbaum demands proof of the border gunfire at the Coast Guard as 500 U.S. troops deploy
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Monday that Mexico has asked Washington for all the evidence of shots allegedly fired from Tamaulipas at U.S. Coast Guard members in Texas in late September, saying her National Guard, Army and Navy detected no fire from the Mexican side. U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson, a former Green Beret, said the threat would be “swiftly addressed” and that the embassy is coordinating with Mexican forces so both countries can patrol their sides of the border. About 500 U.S. troops, with helicopters, drones and anti-drone gear, have deployed since the incident, and Mexico has sent its own forces under a joint effort called Operation Mirror that Sheinbaum said is meant “to forestall any issues.”

stories.headline: Ukraine says its long-range strikes have knocked out 51% of Russia’s oil-refining capacity
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said recent strikes on refineries in Moscow, Yaroslavl, Ust-Luga, Perm, Saratov and Syzran have disabled 51% of Russia’s refining capacity, a claim that could not be independently verified. Russia, historically the world’s third-largest producer of refined fuel, has 32 refineries; some have been hit as many as 15 times, and lately one is struck about every three days, creating a cycle of damage and emergency repairs. In a rare acknowledgment, Vladimir Putin said Oct. 1 the attacks had cost Russia roughly 1% of gross domestic product. Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara called it a significant blow to Moscow’s ability to supply its troops as the 750-mile front line stalls.

stories.headline: British Airways jet bound for Chicago drops 27,000 feet over Ireland and turns back to Heathrow
stories.summary: About 30 minutes after leaving London on Monday, a British Airways flight to Chicago descended from 36,000 feet to 9,000 feet over several minutes, according to FlightAware data, in what appeared to be a controlled descent. The airline cited a technical issue. The plane turned around over Ireland and circled for a few hours, apparently to burn off fuel, before landing safely back at Heathrow on Monday evening, where passengers got off normally and BA said it was working to rebook them.

stories.headline: Malkin breaks his game-day silence to salute Ovechkin’s retirement plan before the Penguins host Winnipeg
stories.summary: Evgeni Malkin broke his usual rule against talking to reporters on a game day to respond to Alex Ovechkin’s announcement that he will retire after the 2026-27 season; Sidney Crosby also spoke about it Monday morning before tonight’s home game against Winnipeg. Drafted first and second in 2004, the two Russians went from rivals to frosty, after a fight involving Malkin’s agent, to mutual respect: Malkin and Crosby gave Ovechkin a Rolex for breaking the goal record, and the two often visit each other’s homes before games. Ovechkin has 929 goals and Malkin 1,411 points, and Malkin has joined Gordie Howe as the only players to open a season at 40 or older with four points in two games. Pittsburgh and Washington meet four times this season, starting Wednesday in D.C.

stories.headline: Jets lose edge Braiden McGregor for the season with a torn pec, thinning the run defense before Browns week
stories.summary: Defensive end Braiden McGregor tore his pectoral muscle in Sunday’s 23–12 loss at Chicago and will miss the rest of the season, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported. The 25-year-old was the fifth man in the edge rotation, with 49 defensive snaps and 45% of special-teams snaps through four games, valued more for setting the edge against the run than for pass rushing. With Kingsley Enagbare also out against the Bears, David Bailey, Will McDonald and Joseph Ossai all played season-high snap shares as Chicago ran for 232 yards. Defensive tackle David Onyemata is also sidelined as the 1–3 Jets prepare to host the 3–1 Browns at MetLife Stadium.

stories.headline: SpaceX shares jump about 5% after Morgan Stanley calls its $300 target ‘cheap’ ahead of Starship Flight 15
stories.summary: SpaceX stock (SPCX) rose about 5.3% to roughly $167 in early trading Monday after Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas reiterated his Outperform rating and $300 price target in a note titled “SPCX $159: Cheap and Getting Cheaper.” Jonas argues investors are fully valuing SpaceX’s space and Starlink businesses but giving little credit to its artificial intelligence push, from compute deals to chipmaking. He called the coming weeks before Starship Flight 15 a “unique opportunity,” citing possible AI product releases, more “neocloud” contracts at $30 to $50 per watt, and Starship progress after Flight 14 reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

stories.headline: Tesla’s German registrations jump 268% in September as Model Y becomes France’s best-selling car
stories.summary: Germany’s Federal Motor Transport Authority reported 12,552 new Tesla registrations in September, up 268.7% from a year earlier, giving Tesla 4.9% of all new cars and about 14.2% of the country’s 88,599 battery-electric registrations. In France, the Model Y was the best-selling car of any kind with 8,183 registrations, edging the Peugeot 208 by 323, and Tesla brand registrations rose 61.9%. Sales tracker Roland Pircher cautioned that the German jump is flattered by a weak September 2025 and end-of-quarter timing, saying Tesla is roughly back to its sales levels of three to four years ago.

stories.headline: Study: Apple News got ‘even more politically lopsided’ in John Ternus’s first month as CEO
stories.summary: A Media Research Center study comparing Apple News in August, Tim Cook’s last month as CEO, with September, John Ternus’s first, found stories from left-leaning outlets rose from 65% to 67% of what the app promoted, while right-leaning outlets fell from 2% to under 1%. MRC President David Bozell said only three stories from right-leaning outlets reached Apple News’s top morning feed in September and called it “blatant discrimination.” The study said Google News and Microsoft’s MSN did not make a similar shift; critics also point to Apple News editor-in-chief Lauren Kern, a former New York Magazine executive editor.

stories.headline: Queen’s Brian May says he is done touring: ‘Maybe 50 years is enough’
stories.summary: Queen guitarist Brian May, 79, told The Times he decided 18 months ago not to tour again, after a close family friend died while the band was in the United States and he realized he couldn’t simply fly home for a few days. He said he loves to play and travel but wants time with his wife, his grandchildren and his astrophysics. May said Queen still wants to do “something fairly revolutionary,” along the lines of ABBA’s avatar show; after seeing the Sphere in Las Vegas he sketched out an immersive Queen show, but he has “serious misgivings” about the artificial intelligence it would currently require.

stories.headline: Aerosmith teases a Hollywood Bowl return on Oct. 29 and Nov. 1, two years after retiring from touring
stories.summary: Aerosmith posted a video Monday of Steven Tyler on a ladder adding letters to the Hollywood Bowl marquee, asking photographer Ross Halfin for an ampersand to spell “Aerosmith & Friends,” with the dates Oct. 29 and Nov. 1. Full details are due Tuesday at 10 a.m. ET. The band retired from touring in August 2024, about a year after the now-78-year-old Tyler fractured his larynx during a September 2023 show; Tyler and Joe Perry last played together at a private April 2025 benefit for Janie’s Fund in San Francisco.

stories.headline: LEGO’s PlayStation Astro Bot gift-with-purchase sells out on LEGO Shop within days
stories.summary: The LEGO PlayStation Astro Bot (40899) promotional set, free with any LEGO Shop purchase of $150 or more, has already sold out online after only a few days. LEGO brand stores may still have it, so call ahead, and some fans grabbed it outright for $24.99 on the PlayStation Store before it sold out there too. Remaining LEGO Shop promotions are the Star Wars Darth Vader’s Lightsaber (40897) gift and double Insiders points on select sets; the Disney Store is offering the lightsaber with $130 purchases using the code FORCE.

stories.headline: That viral ‘Insta360 mirrorless camera’ video looks like an AI hoax, though the company is experimenting
stories.summary: A YouTuber’s video claims Insta360 will unveil two interchangeable-lens cameras at Japan’s CP+ show in late February 2027, but Digital Camera World says the images look AI-generated: the first body’s mount appears identical to Sony’s E-mount, down to the pins, and its styling looks like a blend of Sony bodies and the Canon EOS M6 Mark II, while the second is plainly a white Ace Pro 2 with a Micro Four Thirds mount that likely wouldn’t fit. The fake comes amid real signals, however: co-founder Max Richter has said Insta360 is experimenting with mirrorless cameras and smart glasses, and carefully avoided denying an interchangeable-lens camera. (Photo: a frame from the circulating AI video, not a real product.)

stories.headline: Duluth’s first public Renaissance Faire draws about 5,000 to Lower Chester Park
stories.summary: Lords, ladies and fairies filled Lower Chester Park on Sunday for the first Duluth Renaissance Faire open to the public, after a private soft launch last year. The free, family-friendly event had more than 50 booths, aerial and fire dancing, a trinket-trading stall, Belegarth combat fighters and blacksmiths, with a goal of putting money in local artists’ and musicians’ pockets. Organizer Joshua Carlson said he was inspired 17 years ago by the Twig ren faire, which closed after his first visit, and that his wife finally told him, “Let’s just do it.” Organizers counted about 5,000 visitors and plan to return next year at the renovated Chester Bowl Chalet.

stories.headline: Himes, Republican Goldstein and independent Wesley set an Oct. 19 4th District debate at Westport Library
stories.summary: The three candidates for Connecticut’s 4th Congressional District, which includes Trumbull, will debate from 7 to 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 19 at the Westport Library, hosted by the League of Women Voters with other lower Fairfield County chapters. Democratic incumbent Jim Himes, 60, is seeking a 10th term against Republican Michael Goldstein, 76, an attorney and eye surgeon, and independent Benjamin Wesley, 48, an engineer. The debate is free but requires advance registration, and it will be live-streamed on the library’s YouTube channel. District residents can submit questions through the registration link or by email; Election Day is Nov. 3.
